Prior to the final 2" of the whole intersection, cut or grind off the AC over the concrete cap, and fill with our final 2" layer of asphalt, which creates our T-Cut. DPR will proceed off of this confirmation and release BTM to begin finalizing the engineering judgement and resubmitting the terracotta assembly submittal to capture the modifications. results.question_text: Reference: SLP1 - RFI0893.2 - B1 Balcony Guardrail Added Plate to Embeds Confirmation_R2 SLP1 - RFI0893.1 - B1 Balcony Guardrail Added Plate to Embeds Confirmation_R1 RFI0893.1-SK5, and SK6 Post on: Detail 8/A8.21 Background: Due to missed steel embeds at corners of Level 3 balcony curbs, the steel embeds for the balcony guardrail were set 1' off of correct locations at the SW and SE balconies. To provide an alternative means of attachment for the balcony guardrails where steel embeds are missing, we propose adding steel plates connected to the steel embeds as noted in the attached sketches. Structural confirmation for the proposed remedial solution was confirmed by Jonathan Chen of DES per response to RFI 0893.1. However, after further evaluation of the originally proposed solution it was determined that a new solution was required due to the limited space between the coping cap from the metal panel and the face of the curb. After reviewing the various options that were discussed, it was decided that the most effective solution would be to add a L5x5 angle where the 1 ½” plate cantilevers, next to the L6x7 angle that will get anchored to the side of the curb. This L5x5 would get anchored down to the SOMD and welded to the bottom of the cantilevered plate. This would occur only at the ends of the curbs where the plate is cantilevered. At the corner’s where we have a column concrete curb, we are proposing to use L5x5 angles to omit the anchor bolts at each plate. The top of the L5x5 would get welded to the bottom of the 1 ½” to provide the support needed. These angles would then get anchored down to the existing column concrete curb. Question: Q1. Please review and confirm the revised proposed sketches SK5 and SK6 (showing the addition of the steel plate per RFI 0893 and omitting the anchors) are acceptable per the attached email with Jonathan Chen/DES.

results.question_text: Reference: SLP1 - RFI 2087 - PSD Stair 2 Concrete Landing Cracking Remediation Confirmation Sheet A7.02, E0.02, E2.03 Submittal 3472 - PSD Light Fixture (Product Data) Attached Pictures Background: At the Stair 2 concrete landings of Tiers 3-5, it is being noticed that water is seeping through the cracks and into the installed light fixture below. Per conversations with the SEOR, these cracks appear to be due to shrinkage and temperature and do not raise structural concerns. The installed light fixtures are "wet location rated". "Wet Location Rated" is defined as an electrical enclosure that is "dust tight and watertight against light pressure water spray". With the intense rains and recent power washing activities, the cracks are allowing more water than what the light fixtures are rated for. To fix this issue, DPR has (2) proposed solutions: Option A: Open crack 1/4" to create amplitude and fill with urethane sealant caulking. ROM of $1,000 to complete this scope at all locations. Option B: Traffic Coat concrete landings to seal the cracking. ROM of $50,000 to complete this scope at all locations. Question: Please confirm which option DES/PMA would like to proceed with.
